claims: Muslims use "Eid Mubarak" as a traditional greeting to wish someone a "blessed" or "happy" Eid festival.
"Eid Mubarak" translates to "Blessed Eid" or "Blessed celebration".
"Eid Mubarak" is commonly used during Eid al-Fitr.
"Eid Mubarak" is commonly used during Eid al-Adha.
Eid al-Adha occurs during the Hajj season.
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha are both major Islamic holidays.
Eid al-Fitr celebrates the end of fasting.
Eid al-Adha celebrates the end of the pilgrimage/sacrifice.
"Eid Mubarak" is commonly used by Arab Muslims.
"Eid-e shoma mobarak" is a variation used in Persian, as noted in Wikipedia.
"Eid Mubarak ho" is a variation used in parts of South Asia, as noted in Wikipedia.
The response to "Eid Mubarak" is often "Khair Mubarak".
"Khair Mubarak" wishes goodness upon the person who offered the greeting.
